content.text: The text reviews diseases of the biliary system, liver, portal vein, pancreas, and peritoneum. Gallstones cause hepatic colic—sudden severe radiating pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation, and often jaundice—while obstruction may produce infection, fistulas, liver damage, or intestinal blockage. It describes diagnostic palpation, stool examination, historical treatments, and complications. Portal-vein thrombosis causes rapid ascites, splenomegaly, gastrointestinal congestion, and hemorrhage; suppurative pylephlebitis causes irregular septic fever and liver abscesses. Hydatid cysts enlarge slowly and may cause pressure symptoms, jaundice, or rupture. Pancreatic disorders produce epigastric pain, wasting, fatty stools, jaundice, diabetes, cysts, or cancer. Peritonitis causes diffuse pain, rigidity, distension, vomiting, constipation, and circulatory collapse. Sandra journeyed to the garden, moved to the hallway, and John went back to the garden.
